title: Request Archiving & Redaction Strategy Sync - HybridPower

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-07
Time: 11:00 AM ET (45 minutes)
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Leo (Redwood SE), Oliver (HybridPower Eng Mgmt), Priya (SecOps), Darren (Platform SRE), Sofia (Legal), Alex (ML)

Summary (auto): Quick demo of Redwood's request storage toggles, redaction pipelines, and archiving modes. Discussed PII handling, customer-managed keys, and what a short POC could look like.

[00:00:05] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Um, quick intros and then we'll jump into the console and the API flows.
[00:00:12] Oliver (HybridPower): Yep, thanks. I'm Oliver — I run the field services infra, curious mostly about request logs and what you can purge or keep.
[00:00:18] Priya (SecOps): Priya here. Want to understand retention, redaction accuracy, and our ability to force-delete requests on demand.
[00:00:25] Maya: Great. Leo and I will share screen, walk through the Request Storage settings in Console, then hit the API behaviors and an Optimize recommendation quick tour.
[00:00:34] Leo (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll start with the Console. First slide — there's three primary modes: Ephemeral (no persistent request storage), Short-term (configurable TTL, e.g., 7-90 days), and Archive (encrypted storage with longer retention and export).
[00:00:52] Darren (SRE): How's Archive different from just dumping to our S3? Like is it searchable? Indexable?
[00:00:59] Leo: Good question. Archive is encrypted at rest with optional CMK, uses our blob store but exposes policy-driven search and redaction pipelines. You can export blobs to your storage but Redwood keeps a managed index that supports retrieval and redact-on-read. It's not identical to raw S3 dump.
[00:01:18] Alex (ML): When you say redact-on-read, is the redaction deterministic? What's the PII detector model and false positive rate?
[00:01:25] Leo: We use a hybrid approach — deterministic pattern matchers for common tokens plus an ML classifier for contextual entities. Typical redaction recall is in the high 90s on enterprise corpora, but precision can vary with domain terms; we recommend a short calibration step in the POC with your sanitized logs.
[00:01:46] Priya: We need audited deletion. If a user exercises GDPR right-to-be-forgotten, can we guarantee purge across backups/archives?
[00:01:54] Maya: Yes, there's an ejection workflow — delete request ID -> triggers purge job that removes from index and marks blobs for shredding. With Dedicated or Private deployments we can also provide an escrow process. Important caveat: in hosted mode backups have a TTL too, but retention windows are transparent in compliance docs. We'll send the specifics.
[00:02:12] Sofia (Legal): Also need a chain-of-custody and logs for deletion ops. Do you capture audit events for who initiated deletions and when?
[00:02:20] Leo: Audit logs are enabled per-tenant. They record actor, method (API/Console), request IDs, and outcome. Logs can be pushed to your SIEM or retained in our audit store depending on plan.
[00:02:33] Oliver: What about encryption keys — can we use our KMS/HSM? We can't have provider-managed keys for some of our datasets.
[00:02:41] Maya: Yes. For Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed keys. For Hosted, we support BYOK through KMS integration where you can rotate keys and we don't retain plaintext. There's an HSM-backed option for enterprise.
[00:02:54] Priya: Any difference in how redaction runs when using CMK? And performance impacts?
[00:03:00] Leo: CMK doesn't change redaction logic; it's just key control for encrypt/decrypt. There is a tiny overhead on archive/decrypt ops during retrieval — typically sub-50ms per file in our benchmarks — but overall token-generation latencies are unaffected because redaction before generation uses streaming transforms.
[00:03:18] [00:03:20] Alex: Can you show the toggle in the Console? I want to see the workflow for switching a model route to ephemeral for a subset of traffic.
[00:03:27] [screen share] Leo: Sure, here's the Routes page. We have per-route Request Storage policies — you can attach a policy to a route by environment, or by API key. Example: dev-route = ephemeral, prod-route = short-term 30 days, compliance-route = archive + CMK + redaction-level=aggressive.
[00:03:50] Priya: Aggressive redaction — what does that mean in practice? Does it strip whole sentences or just tokens?
[00:03:56] Leo: Configurable. Aggressive mode will redact full spans that match PII entities and optionally obfuscate tokens using deterministic hashes if you want token-level linkage without exposing raw values. Conservative mode redacts only high-confidence tokens. There's also a review queue for borderline cases.
[00:04:12] Darren: For our performance-sensitive streams, how does ephemeral mode affect caching and KV cache reuse? We use long conversations with many tokens.
[00:04:20] Leo: Ephemeral storage means requests aren't written to long-term blob store, but runtime-level KV cache and prefix caching still operate in-memory for the session. So latency and cache efficiency remain. The only tradeoff is you don't get persisted request history for later analysis.
[00:04:36] Oliver: If we want some subset of requests kept but redacted, can Redwood do incremental masking so ML teams can still see non-PII context?
[00:04:44] Leo: Yes — you can configure field-level retention. For JSON requests we support a schema-based masking policy where certain fields are always redacted, others are pseudonymized, and others kept. The Optimize module can suggest fields to mask based on token contribution to cost and downstream ML utility.
[00:05:02] [00:05:10] Maya: Quick pause — a few of you asked about the POC. Our proposal: 7-10 day bench where Leo runs redaction accuracy tests on a sanitized sample set, and we measure latency impact under representative load. We'll also exercise the delete and ejection workflows and show audit logs.
[00:05:25] Priya: That sounds reasonable. Will Redwood need network-side access to our VPC for the Appendix tests?
[00:05:31] Maya: For Private or Dedicated yes; for Hosted we can do a hybrid where you push samples to a secure transfer bucket and we run the tests. If you prefer private connectivity, we can set up a short-term peered test environment.
[00:05:44] Sofia: Legal question — for the POC, what's the data retention on Redwood's side for the sanitized samples? We need contract language.
[00:05:51] Maya: We propose a 30-day POC retention by default for samples, but can shorten it and include explicit deletion triggers in the MSA. We'll include those clauses in the packet.
[00:06:02] Alex: Any out-of-the-box tools for measuring redaction FP/FN? We want metrics we can sign off on.
[00:06:08] Leo: We provide an evaluation harness that outputs precision/recall against a labeled set, and also a human-in-the-loop review queue for ambiguous items. We'll share the harness repo as part of the POC artifacts.
[00:06:20] Oliver: Let's talk about search and e-discovery. If an auditor requests items, can we run redaction at query-time so auditors only see permitted fields?
[00:06:29] Leo: Yes, role-based query-time redaction is supported. You can define auditor roles that get unredacted access, or you can provide pre-redacted exports. All accesses are logged.
[00:06:38] Priya: On the subject of cost — archive storage vs short-term — can you provide unit economics? Our CFO will ask about $/GB + per-retrieval costs.
[00:06:45] Maya: We'll include a cost sheet in the follow-up. Generally archive has lower per-GB storage cost and an extra per-retrieval fee; short-term is higher storage but no retrieval surcharge. Also Optimize can suggest TTLs and quantization that lower token unit costs overall.
[00:06:59] Darren: How do rollouts behave if we flip a route from short-term to ephemeral mid-flight? Are in-flight requests lost?
[00:07:06] Leo: Flips are policy changes going forward. In-flight requests complete against the policy active at the time of ingestion. You can also trigger a backfill purge job to remove previously stored requests if needed.
[00:07:18] Sophia (Legal): Spell of quick note — you mentioned audit logs could be pushed to our SIEM. Are they in a structured format?
[00:07:25] Leo: Yes, JSON lines with schema, timestamps in ISO, actor, request_id, action, outcome, and optional metadata.
[00:07:32] [00:07:45] Alex: A bit of a tangent: do you have example integrations with key rotation processes? We have a strict rotation cadence — keys rotate every 90 days.
[00:07:54] Leo: We support key rotation with zero-downtime for CMKs; new archives are encrypted with the new key and we keep a key back-compat map to decrypt older blobs. For HSM we integrate with rotation APIs; we can document the exact API calls.
[00:08:12] Maya: Ok, let's demo an actual redaction run. Leo, can you trigger a sample request with PII and show console logs?
[00:08:18] Leo: Yep. Sending sample — here's payload: {name: "J. Carter", account: "AC-12345", notes: "call 555-0134, ssn 123-45-6789"}.
[00:08:29] [00:08:33] Leo: Console shows ingestion -> redaction pipeline executed -> result stored in archive with redactions applied: ssn replaced with [REDACTED], phone hashed as phone_hash: "ph_3a2f". There's an audit event with actor "demo-user" and request_id.
[00:08:47] Priya: Can we tune the phone hashing to be reversible for us only?
[00:08:51] Leo: Reversible pseudonymization can be done with customer keys — we can store mapping encrypted with your CMK so only you can reverse in-house.
[00:08:58] Oliver: Performance numbers on that demo?
[00:09:02] Leo: Redaction pipeline stepped in at ~120ms on this sample, archive write at ~40ms extra. Under heavy load we saw pipeline median around 150-250ms depending on complexity. We'll include load numbers in the benchmark.
[00:09:15] [00:09:18] Alex: For our ML use case, often we want token-level but anonymized traces for model retraining. Can Optimize suggest what to keep to preserve model fidelity while saving cost?
[00:09:27] Leo: Absolutely. Optimize analyzes token contribution to loss and suggests field-level pseudonymization or selective retention. It can also recommend quantized model variants and batching settings to lower per-token cost.
[00:09:39] Priya: One nit — does any data ever leave region? We need EU residency for some customers.
[00:09:46] Maya: Region controls are per-tenant. You can pin storage and compute to regions; cross-region replication is opt-in. We'll include region-residency language.
[00:09:56] Oliver: What about our edge collectors — we don't want to change the SDK much. Can you work with us on SDK flags to mark sensitive fields client-side?
[00:10:03] Leo: Yes, we have client-side masking hooks and pre-ingest filters. Those can be toggled per-API key so your SDKs can annotate fields as "sensitive" for server-side redaction to respect.
[00:10:14] [00:10:22] Maya: Ok wrapping up — quick recap and next steps. We will send SOC2/ISO evidence, KMS integration notes, POC plan with the evaluation harness, and a cost sheet. You (HybridPower) will prepare a sanitized sample set and pick two routes to test: one ephemeral and one short-term 30-day archived route with CMK.
[00:10:41] Oliver: Sounds good. Any blockers from our side? I think Priya will want the security deep-dive scheduled before the POC starts.
[00:10:48] Priya: Yes, please.
[00:10:50] Maya: We'll get that scheduled. Thanks everyone.

Action items in-conversation:
- Maya: send security artifacts & cost sheet (see next steps)
- Leo: prepare POC harness + scripts
- Alex/Oliver: provide sanitized sample set

End of transcript.
